newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Bullish US T-bonds may relent near term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bullish US T-bonds may relent near term.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures, which have seen scant correction during their 2-1/2 month rally, may at last be showing signs of relenting, technical analysts said.

Channel resistance was effectively containing the topside, the daily stochastic was faltering in overbought territory, and moving average convergence/divergence (MACD) histogram was showing a strong bearish divergence, said Scott Siller, a senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch.
"Those three elements combined are what I consider a perfect signal," Siller said.
By connecting the April and late-May lows and drawing a parallel line from the May highs on September futures' daily chart, a clear bull channel could be drawn, he noted.

"Sure enough, we project a 10-week bull channel resistance and the market's hit it perfectly at 112-24/32 (last Friday)," he said. "So there is good reason for the market to correct now and stay within this trend slope."
The positive spread on the MACD has been making lower tops during the recent bond market rally and was now sliding into negative territory, he added.
The daily stochastic was also marking a subtle bearish divergence as it began heading down, although it was not a "class-A" divergence, he said.
Siller expected the 111-area, the 38 percent Fibonacci retracement of the 2-1/2 month rally, would be the minimum objective for a pullback.
The 62 percent retracement at about 110, coinciding with channel support, was obviously a critical level, he added.
Stewart Taylor, president of Taylor Consulting, agreed that unusually strong overbought signals needed to be addressed.
"The market hasn't done anything overtly bearish yet, but there is a huge overbought condition in terms of the daily oscillators," he said.
He added that the rally in recent weeks had been accompanied by a decline in open interest, suggesting that it was fuelled by short-covering, not necessarily by growing fresh demand.
He said one measure of the market's most recent upward bias was a steep uptrend on the hourly chart, on which support now came in at around 111-23/32.

"If you close below that uptrend, that would represent a fairly significant change in the bond market's behavior," Taylor said, adding that a finish below 111-17/32 support would be even more negative.
He said he would anticipate a few days to a few weeks of consolidation if a near-term peak was confirmed.
